subject: Re: Materiality & pricing tunnel language — packaging interaction redlines

Subject: Pricing exhibit redlines — materiality thresholds & packaging interaction

Hi Mina,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Our GC and finance team reviewed the pricing exhibit and pushed back on two items that are blocking the deal on our side:

1) "Tunnel rate" resets — the language as written allows a mid-term reset based on usage variance without a clear materiality threshold. We need something that prevents frequent micro-resets.
2) Packaging parity / SKU reclassification — the clause that lets Redwood reclassify SKUs and apply floors retroactively is concerning. Finance wants assurance that packaging changes only affect forward billing (not retro).

I've attached our redline (Novus_Exhibit_Pricing_v3_redline.pdf) with comments. Can your legal and deals team propose narrow alternative language that preserves your ability to rebalance but addresses our materiality and non-retroactivity concerns?

If useful, Sam (cc'd) can join a quick working call — we're available tomorrow morning PST.

Best,
Elena Torres
Sr. Head of Revenue Ops | NovusPlatform

On Thu, Nov 5, 2026 at 8:03 AM Elena Torres <elena.torres@novusplatform.com> wrote:
> Thanks for sending the draft order form. Our GC and finance team reviewed the pricing exhibit and pushed back on two items ...

Elena — thanks for the clear notes and the annotated redline. Appreciate Sam offering time; we should lock a short working session.

Quick responses to the two points so we have alignment before legal swaps language:

1) Tunnel resets / materiality: We agree that frequent small resets are bad for both sides. Redwood is willing to accept a materiality floor that gates automatic tunnel retuning. Proposed operational text (high level): "Tunnel rate adjustments may only be triggered if observed billable usage deviates from the contracted baseline by at least 15% in two consecutive billing months, or 20% in a single month in the event of verifiable anomaly detection; adjustments apply prospectively." I've attached a draft suggestion with inline language.

2) Packaging / SKU reclassification: We can commit to non-retroactive application of reclassifications. Our intent is to reprice future orders and to apply grandfathering for completed invoices. Suggested wording: "Changes to SKU classification will only apply to bookings or invoices issued after the effective change date; no retroactive increases to previously billed amounts."

Operational caveats: we still need the ability to preserve reserved capacity economics (if a customer moves volume into a lower-priced package that undermines capacity commitments, we will reserve the right to true-up or re-negotiate commit levels). That can be handled via a separate true-up paragraph and a 30-day notice window.

Attachments: redline_suggestion_mh.docx (Word suggested edits). I'm looping legal (Markus) and deals (Marissa/Karthik) — can you confirm whether Novus is okay with the 15% / 2-month gate or would prefer a lower threshold? If you prefer, we're open to meeting tomorrow 09:00-10:00 PST.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redline_suggestion_mh.docx (DOCX, 18KB)

Mina — quick internal note: 15% x 2-month is probably defensible commercially, but Ops will push back on anything that lets customers game the window. Suggest we offer 12% sustained (two-month) or 15% single-month spike with anomaly carveouts. Keeps it customer-friendly but reduces noise. Also want billing-ops (cc not included) to confirm how true-ups would settle (invoice vs credit).

Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit redlines — materiality thresholds & packaging interaction

Elena / Sam — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the annotated PDF. After internal coordination with legal and deals, here's a short summary of the agreeable redline positions and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

1) Tunnel / materiality gate (agreed preliminary): Redwood proposes a measurable gate for automated tunnel adjustments of "sustained >=12% deviation from contracted baseline over two consecutive billing months, or >=15% in a single month conditioned on verified anomaly flags". Tunnel adjustments will be applied prospectively and not retroactively.

2) Packaging / SKU reclassification (agreed preliminary): Any SKU or packaging reclassification will be non-retroactive and will only apply to bookings or invoices with an effective date after the change. Redwood reserves the right to discuss commit-level true-ups if the reclassification materially reduces reserved capacity economics; true-ups will be subject to a 30-day notice and will settle on the next invoice cycle (credit or invoice depending on Ops workflow).

3) Operational tie-outs: We're proposing one short working call to confirm definitions (how baseline is calculated, what counts as anomaly, and the operational flow for true-ups). Proposed times: 11/06 14:00-14:30 PST or 11/07 09:00-09:30 PST.

4) Next legal step: Markus will produce a tracked-changes amendment reflecting the two bullets above and the true-up clause; we'll post to the DocuSign draft link and share a Drive folder.

If that high-level summary matches Novus's intent we're happy to have Markus circulate the formal amendment. I've attached a one-page summary for convenience.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
